headline: Chromatin architecture from nucleosomes to multiway contacts shapes regulatory output
label: Genomic Context Of Regulatory Elements
summary: Long-read footprints, kilobase compartments and multiway Hi-C/Micro-C models now resolve regulatory activity at multiple chromatin scales.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that regulatory activity is interpreted within its three-dimensional and nucleosome-level context rather than treated as isolated sequence. CRUSH refines A/B chromatin compartments to 1 kb at low sequencing depth, revealing micro-compartments across cell types, single cells, and an ancient mammoth sample. A polymer-physics ensemble model built from Hi-C and Micro-C contact maps, combined with an Activity-by-Multiway-Contact model, links multiway enhancer-promoter interactions to gene expression changes in cancer. IDLI classifies long-read single-molecule footprints to show pervasive nucleosome distortion and transcription factor-linked regulation of chromatin on individual fibres. What is new is the treatment of architecture across scales, from single-fibre nucleosome states to kilobase compartments and multiway contacts, as an explicit determinant of regulatory output.
